result.summary: The image shows a residential intersection with basic pedestrian infrastructure including sidewalks and a marked crosswalk across the side street. However, the environment lacks traffic calming measures, and sightlines are partially obstructed by parked vehicles and utility poles.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstruction
hazards.description: Trash bags and bins are placed on the sidewalk on the left side of the image, narrowing the path for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles near the intersection corners and a utility pole at the immediate corner limit sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs at the corners to shorten the pedestrian crossing distance and improve visibility by preventing parking too close to the intersection.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Upgrade the existing parallel line crosswalk to a continental or ladder pattern to increase its visibility to approaching motorists.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to ensure clear sightlines for both pedestrians and drivers.

result.summary: This residential street lacks basic pedestrian infrastructure, with no marked crossings and a sidewalk that is narrow and partially obstructed by fencing. Pedestrians on the left side of the image are forced to walk on the grass or in the roadway due to the absence of a paved walkway and the presence of debris.

hazards.name: Discontinuous/Obstructed Sidewalk
hazards.description: The sidewalk on the right is narrow and encroached upon by a fence, while the left side has no sidewalk at all, forcing pedestrians into the street.

hazards.name: Debris and Obstructions
hazards.description: Trash bags and bins are placed on the shoulder where a pedestrian would walk, creating a tripping hazard and forcing movement into traffic lanes.

hazards.name: Poor Roadway Condition
hazards.description: The asphalt is cracked and shows signs of significant wear, which can be a tripping hazard for pedestrians crossing the street.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Completion
interventions.description: Install continuous, ADA-compliant sidewalks on both sides of the street to separate pedestrians from vehicular traffic.

interventions.title: Street Lighting Installation
interventions.description: Add pedestrian-scale street lighting to improve visibility and safety during nighttime hours.

interventions.title: Marked Crosswalks
interventions.description: Paint high-visibility crosswalks at the nearest intersection to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by a wide, unmarked parking lot entrance that lacks sidewalk continuity and crossing infrastructure. Pedestrians are forced to navigate a large, unprotected conflict zone with vehicles without the aid of markings, signs, or dedicated paths.

hazards.name: Wide Unmarked Driveway
hazards.description: A very wide entrance to a parking lot lacks any markings or designated space for pedestrians, creating a large conflict zone.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground where the driveway meets the street.

hazards.name: Lack of Sidewalk Continuity
hazards.description: The sidewalk on the right ends abruptly at the driveway, forcing pedestrians into the vehicle path.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the driveway entrance.

hazards.name: Degraded Pavement
hazards.description: Cracked and uneven asphalt at the driveway entrance creates potential trip hazards for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Raised Pedestrian Crossing
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk across the driveway as a raised crossing to maintain pedestrian priority and slow entering/exiting vehicles.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk Markings
interventions.description: Paint a high-visibility crosswalk across the driveway entrance to alert drivers to the presence of pedestrians.

interventions.title: Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Install ADA-compliant curb ramps where the sidewalk meets the driveway to ensure accessibility.

result.summary: The image shows a residential intersection with sidewalks and curb ramps but lacks marked crosswalks or traffic control devices. The wide, unmarked roadway and parked vehicles near the corner create potential visibility and speed-related risks for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crossing
hazards.description: The intersection lacks painted crosswalks, which fails to designate a clear path for pedestrians or alert drivers to their presence.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Vehicles
hazards.description: Vehicles parked close to the intersection on the left side of the street may block sightlines between pedestrians and approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the street, mid-ground

hazards.name: Wide Unmarked Roadway
hazards.description: The lack of lane markings on a relatively wide street can encourage higher vehicle speeds and unpredictable positioning.
hazards.location_in_image: Main roadway stretching into the background
